images.caption: Figure 1:The same verdict from different cited evidence. (a) Reference and candidate tool states are supplied to the same agent model on healthy hardware. Claim 431 concerns ROS-mediated FoxO3a activation in neuronal death. Gemma’s reference branch cites a sentence about ROS and autophagy (19922508/3), and its candidate branch cites ROS sensing microbe size (22696649/1). Neither sentence supports the stated FoxO3a mechanism, yet both branches return the benchmark-correct SUPPORT label. Neither citation matches the annotated evidence, 28937856/5. Sentence indices are zero-based and document identifiers are SciFact IDs. (b) Restoration and transplantation select values at their original coordinates. (c) Tool execution completion, evidence-path fidelity, and verdict correctness are evaluated. H1 and H2 repeat the same reference state.

Figure 2:Read and citation selections across repeated batches. (a) Actual document and sentence selections. Qwen reads the same document without citing under C; both NEI verdicts are wrong. Gemma gives correct verdicts while selecting different evidence, neither branch matching the annotated evidence. (b) Each marked combination has stable within-state endpoints, different H/C endpoints, and full restoration in all eight batches. Figure3reports all attempts and incomplete groups.

Figure 3:All attempts and within-state variability. (a) Each model schedules 27 combinations×\timeseight batches×\timesseven conditions, or 1,512 episodes. (b) Qwen has 208 jointly completed groups and Gemma 152. Between candidate and H1, read, citation, and verdict discordances are 1, 25, and 0 for Qwen and 32, 35, and 0 for Gemma; H2 and full restoration never differ from H1. (c) Claim 507 differs only in the seventh batch; its adjusted read difference is zero. (d) Summaries weight each of 26 Qwen and 20 Gemma combinations equally. CH, HH, and CC are between-state and within-state discordance fractions;δ=CH−(HH+CC)/2\delta=\mathrm{CH}-(\mathrm{HH}+\mathrm{CC})/2, in percentage points (AppendixH.12).

Figure 4:Recovery under score and prefix interventions. (a) Recovery for the compound-activity model across nine tested budgets and two changed captures. Random priority averages 128 fixed orders. Horizontal spacing uses log2(b + 1), but the AUC in TableC1is computed over b/127. Percentages of remaining differences refer to the two-block budget. (b) Two baseline Qwen repeats for claim 431: one score is restored and 95 differences remain. Citations and verdict recover, reads do not, and transplantation does not reproduce the candidate verdict. (c) Citation discordances after prefix interventions in 24 groups. Healthy repeat has 2/24 discordances.

Figure 5:Changed hERG assay allocations and recovery. (a) BF16 predictions feed native Biomni selection and triage; R1 recomputes predictions flagged by arithmetic checks, and R1+M adds a margin rule that also recomputes 68 compounds near decision boundaries. (b) Changed decisions across 16 sources; the ring marks the discrepancy left by R1 and recovered by R1+M. Healthy margin is distance to the affected decision’s boundary; lower rows show recovery and the decisions of native Biomni runs on R1+M inputs. (c) Prediction displacement versus healthy distance to the nearer boundary; highlights mark changed decisions, and the lower strip shows entry with unchanged predictions. (d) R1 residual versus the minimum decision margin computed from R1 scores; shading marks R1+M selection. Dashed lines in (c,d) mark equality.
